messages.subject: Re: How does packrat deal with packages that depend on having a C++ compiler, esp. Rtools?
messages.subject_clean: How does packrat deal with packages that depend on having a C++ compiler, esp. Rtools?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ben,

Can you elaborate? Packrat does not do very much -- versions of Rtools are tied to versions of R, and we generally rely on the user having Rtools + their PATH appropriately set up for package development on Windows requiring Rtools. Currently, all packrat does re: version of R is store the version of R a particular project uses, and warn if the project is loaded from a session with a different version of R.

FWIW, the RStudio IDE has a lot of tooling built in to automate lookup / use of Rtools.

Cheers,
Kevin

messages.subject: Announcing Packrat 0.4.1-1 on CRAN!
messages.body_plain:
We’re happy to announce that Packrat is now on CRAN, with version 0.4.1-1!

In particular, this release provides better support for local repositories. Local repositories are just folders containing package sources (currently as folders themselves).
One can now specify local repositories on a per-project basis by using:
packrat::set_opts(local.repos = <pathToRepo>)

and then using packrat::install_local(<pkgName>) to install that package from the local repository.

There is also experimental support for a global ‘cache’ of packages, which can be used across projects. If you wish to enable this feature, you can use (note that it is disabled by default):
packrat::set_opts(use.cache = TRUE)

in each project where you would utilize the cache. By doing so, if one project installs or uses e.g. Shiny 0.10.1 for CRAN, and another version uses that same package, packrat will look up the installed version of that package in the cache — this should greatly speed up packrat::init()s for new projects that use projects overlapping with other packrat projects with large, overlapping dependency chains.

In addition, this release provides a number of usability improvements and bug fixes for Windows.

Release notes follow:
Packrat 0.4.1

Coincides with first CRAN release of packrat.

Disabled migration warnings on Windows (as we now use junction points if
possible to facilitate isolation)

Fix bug with tar and projects containing a large number of files (#129)

External packages (alongside their dependencies) are now symlinked to the
packrat/lib-ext folder — this allows external packages to function better
alongside regular packrat workflows.

If package symlinking (junctioning) fails, we instead copy the package to
the corresponding packrat lib* folder.
Packrat 0.4.0

The source.packages argument for init and snapshot has now been
removed. In lieu, projects can now specify local repositories — packages
will be looked up in these directories when attempting to use a source
package.

Added install_local for installing packages from local repositories. For
example, install_local("abc") will attempt to find and install a package
named abc from the local repositories as specified within packrat.opts.

Added option use.cache, for creating a persistent global cache of
installed packages which can be easily symlinked and reused across multiple
projects. When active, this will force installation of one version of a
package only once — thereafter, any projects requiring that package can
symlink to the installed version in the cache.

Use junction points on Windows to enable caching of packages.

Added opts as an object for conveniently getting / setting specific
options. For example, calling opts$auto.snapshot() returns the current
value for the auto.snapshot option, while opts$auto.snapshot(TRUE) sets
auto.snapshot on.

Fixed spurious download.file warnings on Windows.

Errors when installing packages on Windows are now captured and reported to
the user.
​

messages.subject: Re: packrat:::init() fails in existing project
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jeff,

It looks like rgdal has some pretty complex dependencies, and so building it from source is tricky. Packrat detects that you have an out-of-date version of rgdal in your user library, and tries to install the same version of the package (but from source).

You might work around this by updating rgdal in your main library, e.g. in a non-packrat project do:
install.packages("rgdal")

This should download a binary of rgdal from CRAN to use in your (user) library, and then later packrat will see that you have an up-to-date version of rgdal installed and use the same binary from CRAN.

Alternatively, you need to figure out how to get the other rgdal dependencies — but that seems very tricky…

I think this also implies that packrat needs to provide some kind of better handling for ‘hard to compile’ packages, but I am not sure what the best behavior is here.

Thanks,
Kevin
​

messages.subject: Re: Unexpected packrat internet request?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe,

I think I know what’s happening. The automatic snapshot mechanism that packrat uses attempts to do automatic snapshots behind the scenes (ie, after every command entered by a user). This call involves a call to available.packages() at some point in the routine, which forces an internet request to CRAN (we ask CRAN for some dependency information on installed packages). I am guessing that this is tripping your proxy.

In a regular R session, the information would be cached per-session — so the first time you call available.packages() I would expect the proxy pop-up; any subsequent calls in the same session should use the cached information. The problem with the automatic snapshot — we actually spawn a new R process to perform the snapshot, and this current doesn’t use the cached available.packages() information — hence necessitating an internet request on every expression.

I would recommend keeping opts$auto.snapshot(FALSE) for now; and I will try to produce the appropriate fix for packrat soon as well.

Thanks,
Kevin

messages.body_plain:
Hi Paolo,

Right now, packrat doesn't do anything particularly special with the version of R it records -- when you start a new R session, packrat will double-check its version against that in the stored project lockfile, and just provide a warning if it doesn't match. Otherwise, everything else will proceed as-is.

The packrat private library is segmented in such a way that each version of R gets its own library, so you shouldn't have to worry about collisions there.

Thanks,
Kevin

> 2. Rebuild a project's library remotely with packrat::restore()

as necessary. This is useful, as you've seen, for build systems and the like.

Kevin

messages.body_plain:
I will be using a Shiny app with about 180 students this fall. Having everyone use the same package versions should help avoid a lot of problems. I stumbled onto miniCRAN and, at least in testing, it works as intended. A first script, run only by me, creates a local repo with binaries for windows and mac (see 1st link below). The shiny app is not in an R-package but is distributed simply as a set of code, data, and markdown files using a read-only dropbox folder. When students first start the app the appropriate binary packages in the local repo (i.e., in their own copy of the dropbox folder) are installed in the local user folder (see 2nd link below).

It is really nice that packrat is included in Rstudio. I would be interested in using it but I really *do not* want students to have to compile packages from source when binary packages are available. Perhaps this is an overly broad question but is it possible to achieve something like what I described above using Packrat?

messages.subject: Re: version control of unspecified files
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tim,

All of the 'packrat/lib*' folders should normally be ignored (and packrat should add to the .gitignore automatically) Any other files within the packrat directory should typically be included in version control, although in some cases you might want to exclude package sources.

It's highly advisable that you include `packrat.opts` and `packrat/init.R` under version control as well -- `packrat.opts` gives project-specific options that you would like to preserve over time, while `packrat/init.R` contains the logic that bounces an R session into packrat mode when R is launched in the project folder.

Thanks,
Kevin

messages.subject: Re: packrat with binary packages only
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,

I think something like this would be achievable, but we currently do not have the functionality to directly support this. Are you thinking that we would have packrat:

1. Work with miniCRAN, so that binaries are downloaded from that repository?
2. Prefer binary versions of CRAN packages, even if the version currently installed does not match the system installed version?

If packrat sees that the repository is set to use `miniCRAN`, then it should prefer downloading binary packages from that repo when possible on `packrat::init` or `packrat::restore`. I would imagine that using something like

    options(repos = c(CRAN = <pathToMiniCRAN>))

should help packrat look for binary packages in the right place; however we might need some more functionality in packrat so that it prefers binary packages on init (when the version of a package in the user library does not match that of the external repository).

Thanks,
Kevin
